contracts.name: MidwayBuyer
contracts.notice: Application-facing front door for FWA pack acquisition, status, settlement, and reward         claims. The only address an integrator indexes.

functions.notice: Acquires one FWA pack for the caller's application under the application's saved         settlement default. Quotes inside the call and returns ETH above the quote to the         caller.
Acquires with an explicit settlement default for this request. `autoSettleEth` true         lets a permissionless caller drive the request to ETH; false keeps the outcome for         the account.
Drives each request to its terminal outcome. Permissionless. Reads no price.
Whether NFT delivery is available for this request, and why not when it is not.
Claims accrued FWA rewards for each request. The engine derives the swap bound from         pool spot; `minOut` may only tighten it. Permissionless.

Claims closed-epoch FWA purchaser rewards. Permissionless: the destination is the         registry-named recipient of each request's application and no caller can redirect it.         `midwayRequestIds[i]` is claimed for `epochs[i]`; repeat an id to claim several epochs.
The epoch a request's acquisition landed in, whether that epoch has closed, and the         request's share in it.

functions.dev: Reads the delivered collection and token id from the request's incident record when one      exists (a recovered forced or stuck asset), otherwise from FWA's listing (a fulfilled      allocation).

functions.notice: Sets this request's `autoSettleEth` to true. One way; reverts `AlreadyManaged` when         it is already true. Account or account operator.
The single action a caller should take on this request now.

Pays each application's full `kind` pot out to its registry-named recipient.         Permissionless: the recipient is resolved by the registry, not by the caller. Skips         an application whose pot is empty.
Price of one acquisition: FWA fee, VRF fee, Midway fee, and their total.
Whether `account` can acquire right now, and whether a FWAT payout can move at all.
Classifies each request whose FWA outcome was forced and records the resulting         incident. Permissionless; called by Midway's keeper.
Recovers an NFT stuck on a request's clone into the request's incident record.         Permissionless; called by Midway's keeper.
Route pinned to `midwayRequestId` at acquisition. Zero `engine` means no such request.
Everything an application reads about one request, in one call.
Recovers ETH mis-sent to the router. Sends the full balance: the router never holds         ETH as part of an acquisition, so any balance here is stray.
Recovers an ERC721 mis-sent to the router.

Recovers an ERC20 mis-sent to the router. The router holds no protocol funds itself;         every acquisition's ETH and reward flow routes through the engine, request buyer, and         reward vault instead.
Retries a pending Shared Upside activity record for each request. Permissionless;         called by Midway's keeper.
Settles for ETH: accepts FWA's depositor bid and pays the recorded account.         Permissionless; the payout target is the snapshotted account.

Settles for FWAT under the caller's own `minOut` and deposits the result into the         application's RewardVault pot. Account or account operator. Reverts         `FwatSettlementUnavailable` when the RewardVault is not a FWAToken distributor.

functions.dev: Every batched lifecycle verb below splits ids across the distinct engines they route      to, calls each engine once, and zips the per-engine `LifecycleOutcome[]` results back      into original call order via `_distinctEnginesIndexed` and a per-engine cursor. No      verb makes a view call into the engine; every emitted event reads only the outcome the      engine already returned.

functions.notice: Withdraws the fee-reserve refund of each finalized request to its recorded account.

contracts.name: MidwayRegistry
contracts.notice: Registers applications and their authorized purchasing accounts. An application has one         admin and any number of bound accounts; a bound account may name one operator to drive         its account-only Buyer calls without holding the account's own key.

functions.notice: Recipients, referrer, and the default `autoSettleEth` snapshotted into a request at         `acquireFor`. A later change to any of these never touches a live request.

Deterministic sentinel pot address for one application and reward kind. Carries no         code and no key; `RewardVault` attributes a balance to it and `payout` later resolves         and pays the recipient this registry names at call time.
The account's own status flag, independent of its application's allowlist state.         Never reverts: an unbound account simply reads `false`.
Whether `applicationId` may acquire under the curated allowlist or open access, on         its own, independent of any one account's status.

Registers an application with `msg.sender` as its admin. `account == msg.sender`         binds the account immediately, since the caller already proves control of it.         `account == address(0)` registers with no bound account. Any other nonzero address is         invited and binds on `acceptApplication`, the path for a contract account deployed         after registration.

Schedules the timestamp at which any registered application may acquire without an         explicit allowlist entry. Operator, once: a plain future timestamp with no relation         to any other contract's cycle schedule.

Authorizes `operator` to make `account`'s account-only Buyer calls. Callable by the         account itself or the admin of `account`'s bound application. Zero clears it. The         operator cannot acquire, cannot change the account binding, and cannot change any         recipient.
Sets the default `autoSettleEth` `MidwayBuyer.acquire()` uses when the caller         supplies none. Existing requests keep their snapshot.

contracts.name: FwaEngineV1
contracts.notice: Midway's FWA integration: turns a funded `acquireFor` call into an FWA pack purchase and         drives that request to settlement, NFT delivery, or refund.

functions.notice: Acquires one pack for `account`. The FWA fee quoted here becomes FWA's own cap, so no         caller derives a cap and no reverse derivation exists to get wrong.

Acquire-pacing signals read from FWA. A keeper sees a nonzero `unfulfilledVrf` when         FWA's VRF subscription cannot yet underwrite another callback and should call         `processAcquisitions` and wait before requesting again.
Whether the recorded account may take delivery of the request's NFT.
Claims each request's accrued surcharge allowance. The bound is derived here, not by         the caller: `minOut` may only tighten it, never loosen it.

functions.dev: Returns `amounts` parallel to `midwayRequestIds` so the Buyer can emit one      `MidwayRewardsClaimed` per id; an id repeated for several epochs sums into one entry.

functions.notice: The epoch a request's acquisition landed in, whether it has closed, and the request's         acquisition count in it (the numerator of its share of that epoch's pot).
Delivers a fulfilled allocation's NFT, or a recovered forced NFT, to `recipient`.
The fee finalization record: measured spend, the charged fee, and the reserve         refund. Zero fields until `EngineRequest.economicsFinalized` is true.

The delivery rule of section 4.2, for callers outside the engine (campaigns,         MegaRip2) that need to route acquisitions or accept auction targets consistently         with what the engine itself will force to ETH settlement.
Amount realized by whichever settlement the request took: ETH proceeds or FWAT.
The incident record for a forced or stuck asset. `detectedAt == 0` means none exists.
Upper bound on `MidwayFeeConfig.midwayFeeBps` this engine accepts. The Buyer         validates its own fee config against this value instead of holding its own cap.
The single action a caller should take on this request now. `callableNow == true`         means the call does not revert in the same block (I11).

Classifies each request whose FWA outcome was forced and records the resulting         incident. Idempotent: a duplicate id's second pass finds the incident already         recorded and nothing left to sweep, so it reports `changed == false`.

Pulls a stuck NFT from FWA into the request's clone and reclassifies it as a         deliverable forced outcome. A duplicate id in the same batch reverts: FWA no longer         names the request's clone as the stuck-NFT recipient after the first recovery.
FWA's settlement and finalize window ends for this request, from the listing's         allocation timestamp. Zero until allocated.

Accepts FWA's depositor bid and pays the recorded account. Unconditional: ETH is         always an acceptable outcome, so any caller may drive a fulfilled request to it. A         duplicate id in the same batch reverts: the second pass is no longer `Fulfilled`.

Accepts FWA's token bid under the caller-supplied `minOut` and deposits the result         into the account's RewardVault pot. Authorization is MidwayBuyer's job; this trusts         `onlyMidwayBuyer`.
Splits funding into the FWA budget and Midway fee reserve.
Withdraws the fee-reserve refund of each finalized request. A duplicate id in the         same batch reverts: `refundWithdrawn` is set on the first pass.

errors.notice: `makeManaged` called on a request whose `autoSettleEth` is already true.
A FWAT settlement or claim attempted while RewardVault is not a FWAToken distributor.

contracts.name: RequestBuyer
contracts.notice: Single-use FWA purchaser for one Midway request.

functions.notice: Settles through FWA's token bid and sends the measured output to RewardVault.

Spends this request's accrued surcharge allowance on FWARewards' token buy and forwards         the output to the RewardVault. The engine derives `minOut` from live pool spot; a zero         bound is refused here so no caller can route an unbounded buy through this clone.

contracts.name: RewardVault
contracts.notice: FWAT custody with measured ingress and address-owned pots.

functions.notice: Pays `amount` of application `applicationId`'s `kind` pot to the recipient the         registry names for that kind now.
functions.dev: Permissionless. The recipient is resolved from the registry at call time and no caller      argument can redirect it, so restricting the caller would protect nothing.

functions.notice: Credit FWAT held by this vault above `totalAttributed` to `pot`. Surplus accumulates         from raw transfers into the vault that never went through `deposit`. Owner only.
Moves `amount` of the caller's own pot to `recipient`.
Pays `amount` of `potAccount`'s own pot to `recipient`. Callable only by         `potAccount`'s registry-authorized account operator.

contracts.name: RewardSplitter
contracts.notice: Splits purchaser rewards three ways: treasury, shared upside, and the application. All         shares stay in RewardVault custody as pot attributions: `RewardVault.payout` resolves and         pays the application share to whoever the registry currently names, so delivery imposes         no requirement on the recipient beyond the pot existing.

functions.notice: Ceiling on the shared-upside share, a fat-finger guard on an economic lever.
Ceiling on the treasury share, a fat-finger guard on an economic lever.
Set the treasury and shared-upside shares together, so the pair stays consistent.         Registry operator only; bounded by `MAX_TREASURY_BPS` and `MAX_SKIM_BPS`.
Set the treasury pot address. Registry operator only; nonzero.

Shared-upside share of gross rewards, in bps. Set at construction; mutable by the         registry operator afterward via `setSplit`. Applies to `split` calls after the change,         never retroactively.

Treasury pot address in RewardVault. Mutable by the registry operator; applies to         `split` calls after the change. FWAT already attributed to the prior address stays in         that pot; moving it onward is the prior treasury's own call.

Treasury share of gross rewards, in bps. Set at construction; mutable by the registry         operator afterward via `setSplit`. Applies to `split` calls after the change, never         retroactively.

contracts.name: SharedUpside
contracts.notice: Weekly-cycle draw over every application's FWAT skim, funded by `RewardSplitter`'s         shared-upside leg. Weight accrues per application per cycle from settlement spend;         `checkpoint` closes a finished cycle and requests a VRF-selected winner weighted by that         cycle's activity, paid the configured share of the cycle's pot.

functions.notice: Time after a cycle ends before `abandonPendingCycle` opens to anyone. Seven days is         `_validateConfig`'s ceiling on `vrfRetryDelay`, so at least one full retry interval         fits inside it under every valid configuration. Measured from `cycleEnd`, which is         fixed: `cycle.requestedAt` moves on every `retryRandomness`, and that call is         permissionless, so a deadline keyed to it could be pushed back indefinitely.

Time after a cycle ends before `checkpoint` will skip it for nothing drawable. Inside         the grace period the call reverts `EmptyDrawablePot` instead, so a checkpoint landing         in the gap between the cycle's end and a pending funding conversion cannot burn the         cycle's draw. One day, well inside the shortest supported funding cadence and short         enough that a genuinely unfunded cycle still clears the cursor promptly.
Maximum number of VRF requests for one cycle, including the initial request.

Give up on a pending cycle's randomness: clears the pending slot, returns the         reserved pot to `drawablePot()`, and marks the cycle `Abandoned`. The cycle's first         randomness request must be at least `cycle.vrfRetryDelay` old for either caller; a         non-owner additionally waits until `ABANDON_AFTER` has elapsed past the cycle's end.
functions.dev: The recovery for a subscription that was deleted, drained, or dropped this contract as a      consumer while a request was in flight. Without it `pendingCycleId` never clears, every      later `checkpoint` reverts `PendingRandomness`, and the reserved pot is stranded.      A callback that arrives afterward is rejected by `fulfillRandomness`'s      `pendingCycleId != cycleId` check, so the pot cannot be paid twice.Both legs are anchored on values no caller can move: `firstRequestedAt` is written once      and `cycleEnd` is fixed. `requestedAt` is not usable here because `retryRandomness` is      permissionless and rewrites it, so a gate keyed to it can be held shut by one retry per      `vrfRetryDelay`.

functions.notice: Closes `cycleId` if it has ended, requesting a VRF-selected winner over its recorded         weight. No-op while `drawsEnabled` is false: there is nothing to close yet.
Migrates a cycle's award into the winning application's `SharedUpsideAward` pot.         `RewardVault.payout` later resolves and pays the current recipient off that pot.
The cycle open at `timestamp`.
functions.dev: Cycle 1 spans `genesisStart` to `cycleStart(2)` as a single span, not a multiple of the      genesis interval schedule's interval: while `drawsEnabled` is false there is no      `cycleStart(2)` yet, so any post-genesis timestamp is cycle 1; once `enableDraws` sets      `cycleStart(2)`, every timestamp before it is still cycle 1 regardless of how many      genesis intervals it spans. Modulo arithmetic over the interval schedule applies only      from cycle 2 onward, where cycles recur on a fixed interval from a fixed start.

functions.notice: Turns on cycle closes. Owner, one way. Schedules cycle 1's close at the next boundary         after this call, using cycle 1's currently configured interval; cycle 2 onward closes         on that same interval going forward.
functions.dev: Before this call `cycleAt` pins every post-genesis timestamp to cycle 1, so any interval      schedule entry queued for cycle 2 or later was never reachable; it is discarded and      replaced with the one computed here.

events.notice: A pending cycle's randomness was given up on. The reserved pot returns to         `drawablePot()` and a late callback for this cycle is rejected.
A cycle closed with nothing drawable, either no eligible weight or an empty pot. No         pot was reserved and the checkpoint cursor advanced.

contracts.name: ChainlinkVrfAdapter
contracts.notice: Immutable Chainlink VRF v2.5 bridge for SharedUpside's cycle/attempt callback ABI.

functions.notice: Allows an ownership transfer to be completed by the recipient.
Get the current owner
Called by SharedUpside after it snapshots a pending cycle and before it stores the returned Chainlink request ID. The adapter snapshots the same cycle/attempt and request config.
Sets the VRF Coordinator addressThis method should only be callable by the coordinator or contract owner
Allows an owner to begin transferring ownership to a new address.
